# Qdrant stored-point reference selection

`lookup.json` contains 52 cases generated by compiling unedited Qdrant functions
at revision `74f3e85b9473c62560006c043e13737ce6b48412` (Apache-2.0).
Paths, source hashes, extracted/harness hashes and function names are in the file.

```sh
rtk proxy .pixi/envs/default/bin/python scripts/qdrant_point_lookup_reference.py
```

The original `ReferencedVectors::get`/`resolve_reference`, input-ID accessor,
reference collection, lookup-name selection and collection-specific reference
selection functions are extracted verbatim. The Rust harness supplies standard
HashMaps, numeric point IDs, dense vector/record types and a nearest-only
`flat_iter` representation. Excluded IDs are deduplicated and sorted for output,
as the upstream filter ultimately converts them into a set. No ranking or vector
search algorithm is implemented in the harness.

The table covers default/self/other/missing collection lookup, default/alternate/
missing fields, missing points and points without the requested vector. Public
tests construct the same real datasets, resolve using the native API and compare
with the upstream resolved-vector and exclusion decisions. Existing native
explicit-vector search provides score regression evidence; it is not represented
as a new independent scoring oracle. Protocol error categories are tested by
their failure condition, not claimed to be HTTP/gRPC compatible status codes.

Additional tests cover all current native scalar/kind combinations, snapshot
ownership, ANN/IVF candidate exclusion, payload filtering, overlays/reopen,
source and target callback-close checks, missing/empty values and query controls.
